status: Source-fit authoring design using three actually prepared attributed cases and unchanged shared claims. No learner attainment or measured conservation outcome is claimed.
reuseDecision: Use resource and impact reasoning with supplied actual case knowledge. The source asks analysis of knowledge informing conservation, not a new fixed project-recall inventory. Australian Country and rainforest claims remain whole and are not relabelled Canadian.

tsouke-own.readScope: Complete actual short main body read, not unread linked PDF or unviewed video.
tsouke-own.facts: Nation’s 2025–2050 plan states teachings, collective voice, values/responsibilities and a seven-generation horizon guiding resources and decisions.
tsouke-own.limits: Do not attribute the current plan’s wording to every older project or every First Nation.

tsouke-attributed-case.locator: Expanding the Scope of a CCP, T’sou-ke Nation; Developing a Collective Vision through Engaging Champions
tsouke-attributed-case.readScope: Actual complete selected community-story section and introductory attribution/acknowledgements read. Not the whole 126-page handbook or figures.
tsouke-attributed-case.sourceRole: Federal handbook expressly presents individual Nations sharing stories; acknowledges T’Sou-ke planner Andrew Moore’s authorship contribution. Partner-published attributed case, not solely a Nation-hosted webpage.
tsouke-attributed-case.facts: Community Elders/youth/families developed a sustainability vision grounded in traditional responsibilities and future generations. It informed solar/hot-water work and a youth-run group encouraging energy conservation; the account also describes teaching traditional food/gathering practices.
tsouke-attributed-case.limits: Distinguish generating renewable energy from reducing consumption. No exact lifetime/output/job/savings percentage, current superlative or proof that all household demand fell is adopted.

tsouke-chief.readScope: Actual textual stewardship/initiative paragraphs read, no signature/map/exhibit visual claim.
tsouke-chief.facts: Then-Chief Gordon Planes explains ancestor-guided ecosystem care for future generations and places solar initiatives within that stewardship account.
tsouke-chief.limits: Historical first-person evidence, not present officeholder, legal/title adjudication, direct technical measurement or wholesale adoption of all affidavit claims.

mno-values.facts: MNO links intergenerational knowledge and Métis ways of life with its Assembly’s harvest policy, conservation/respect for species and Captains supporting harvesters.
mno-values.limits: MNO’s own stated approach, not all Métis law/practice, proof of every population outcome or permission for a pupil to harvest.

mno-practice.locator: Main role/duties/annual-survey text, page updated 2020 with 2024 photo caption
mno-practice.readScope: Complete main body read; photograph not visually assessed and regulations not followed/read.
mno-practice.facts: Captains help implement policy, provide traditional-knowledge information, exchange on-the-ground observations and support surveys of number/species/location of harvest.
mno-practice.limits: Attributable knowledge→monitoring/management role, not a new quota/current legal interpretation or a claim observed counts alone prove conservation success.

inuit-knowledge.locator: 2019 strategy, printed 6/PDF 8 Imappivut example and printed 20–21/PDF 22–23 knowledge priorities
inuit-knowledge.readScope: Actual selected main text read, Imappivut printed 6/PDF 8 rendered and visually read. No all 48 pages or unviewed diagram claim.
inuit-knowledge.facts: ITK describes Nunatsiavut’s2017 marine-planning initiative and2018 community knowledge gathering on local uses/protection priorities. This informs a plan to protect marine life while supporting Inuit use; protected areas were possibilities at that report date.
inuit-knowledge.limits: ITK is Inuit-authored national strategy attributing a Nunatsiavut case; not all Inuit communities or proof that a proposed protected area was established or caused measured ecological recovery.

first-nation.people: T’Sou-ke First Nation, southern Vancouver Island
first-nation.knowledge: Shared Elders/family/community teachings about responsibility to land and future generations, expressed through community planning.
first-nation.action: Solar/hot-water programme and a youth conservation group; distinguish producing renewable energy from encouraging less demand.
first-nation.conservationReasoning: Long-term stewardship values help set priorities and participation for reducing dependence on finite fuels and avoiding unnecessary consumption; no solar panel alone proves Indigenous knowledge was used.
first-nation.evidenceLimit: The attributed account establishes the community process/project and conservation initiative, not an audited reduction for every home.

metis.people: Métis Nation of Ontario’s participating communities/harvesters
metis.knowledge: Intergenerational harvest knowledge, respect/conservation principles and situated observations.
metis.action: Harvest policy, Captains’ advice/implementation, on-the-ground information and annual survey support.
metis.conservationReasoning: Community knowledge and information about species/place/harvest inform management rather than treating resource use as unlimited; explain policy/knowledge/monitoring roles without inventing a quota.
metis.evidenceLimit: A declared principle or reported harvest total is not by itself a measured increase in wildlife populations.

inuit.people: Labrador Inuit communities involved in Nunatsiavut’s Imappivut initiative, as described by ITK in 2019
inuit.knowledge: Community knowledge of marine area uses and protection priorities, with Inuit relationships and needs central to planning.
inuit.action: Gathering local knowledge to develop marine-management choices, including possible protected-area/co-management options.
inuit.conservationReasoning: Knowledge about actual uses and priorities can inform where/how marine resources are protected while sustaining community use; not merely an externally designed map with an Inuit label.
inuit.evidenceLimit: Keep the 2017 launch, 2018 knowledge gathering and 2019 account distinct; no assertion all proposed measures had been enacted or achieved recovery.

protocol.preparation: Provide the original three attributed case cards and exact selected public source sections, with dates, knowledge/action/reason/unknowns columns. No personal disclosure, community contact, sacred teaching, pupil harvesting or invented community testimony.
actions: Actually use ALL THREE cases; identify the named people/place and their knowledge/ways-of-knowing contribution, the concrete action and how it can support energy/resources conservation.

Compare intergenerational responsibilities, harvest observations/management and marine-place knowledge without assuming a single shared practice or that all contemporary methods must be ancient to count.

Distinguish a project owned by an Indigenous organisation from a source-backed contribution of knowledge/values/observations to decisions. Likewise separate announced plans, actual actions and demonstrated outcomes.

Changed fictional brief: a new project uses renewable technology but gives no information about community decision-making or knowledge use. Explain why ownership/technology alone cannot establish the selected source duty; identify needed public attributable evidence.
protocol.positive: Correct named-case knowledge→decision/action→conservation relationship with explicit source/date and limits.
protocol.nearMiss: Names FN/Métis/Inuit or a solar project without explaining knowledge’s role, relabels Australian Country/rainforest knowledge as Canadian, or reports a proposed area as a proven recovery outcome.
protocol.transfer: Explain what source evidence would distinguish a knowledge-informed new conservation decision from a merely labelled/owned project, without inventing or collecting restricted knowledge.

contributionRoles.mt_VI5kdtf28e: Energy-resource origin, renewable/finite distinction and environmental trade-offs contribute particularly to the T’Sou-ke case. No claim that a solar installation alone demonstrates Indigenous knowledge or reduced consumption.
contributionRoles.mt_deexfCHU9m: Action-to-protected-environment mechanisms contribute across all three cases. The source-specific knowledge-to-decision relationship is directly assessed through the actual portfolio, not inferred from generic respect or a link.

wholeClaimBoundary: Natural resources retains its actual multi-source energy origin, renewable/non-renewable and environmental-effect operation; this portfolio alone does not certify that complete topic. Its energy-transfer and resource-vocabulary hard paths remain intact.

Reducing Human Impact retains three local problems, matching solutions, mechanism explanations and communication. Named community case analysis is a component contribution, not a claim that all local whole-topic performance has occurred.

The actual source duty is assessed through use of every First Nation, Métis and Inuit case, knowledge→action→conservation explanations and the changed unsupported brief. Supplied sources may remain available; no invented from-memory project-retention condition is added.
sourceAndPerformanceLimits: Named organisations and dated accounts are attributed separately; no single case represents all peoples.
Plans, reported actions and measured outcomes are different. No protected-area enactment, population recovery, household savings or current officeholder is inferred from these historical accounts.
Resources are prepared public sources, not a requirement to collect private or sacred knowledge. Actual pupil success is unobserved and not asserted.
consumerBoundary: No new ID, authored claim, guide, age interval, dependency or learner state change. These are two existing-topic component associations, with mandatory source-specific performance designed separately.
